transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess... I’m just really tired. Not normal tired. Sleep doesn’t seem to fix it, and even small things like unloading the dishwasher or trying to read for my certificate class feel like too much sometimes.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
I don’t know… maybe a little. I wouldn’t say I’m, like, deeply depressed. Just kind of low and worn out, I guess.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
Yeah… some. I haven’t really cared about the stuff I usually do. Like sketching, cooking, yoga… even going to gallery openings or playing tennis with a friend just feels kind of… pointless right now.
Have you been worrying a lot lately?
Not really… I mean, I think about stuff, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been worrying a lot. At least, not more than usual.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?
I’m not sure… nothing that really stands out. My sleep’s maybe a little off, but I haven’t been paying close attention.
Have you been feeling this loss of interest most days?
Yeah… most days, I think. I just haven’t really cared about the things that usually feel like me—sketching, cooking, yoga… that kind of stuff.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Maybe… about three months? It’s been this quieter stretch for a while now.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living?
I… I don’t really know. I’ve felt pretty low, but I’m not sure I’d put it that way.
Have you had thoughts of killing yourself?
No… I don’t think so. I’ve felt really low, but not… not like that.
Did something stressful happen around the time this started?
Yeah… I think so. It kind of started around when my spouse and I began arguing a lot more. It’s been… maybe four months altogether.
Do you feel this low mainly because of the problems with your spouse?
I don’t know… maybe partly. It’s hard to tell if it’s because of that or if everything just feels heavier lately.
When you and your spouse have a better day, does your mood lift noticeably?
I’m not really sure. Maybe a little sometimes, but I haven’t noticed it being a big, obvious change.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite?
Yeah… it’s been kind of off. Some days I’ll realize I’ve only had coffee and a few bites of something. My jeans are a little looser too, and I wasn’t trying to lose weight.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
Yeah… a bit. I’ll open my planning app and just stare at it, trying to pick between a class assignment, paying a bill, making dinner… and then I don’t do any of it for a while.
Before this started, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed or lost interest in things for at least two weeks?
I… I’m not really sure. I can’t think of a clear time like that, at least not one that stands out.
When the conflict with your spouse eases up, do you feel noticeably less down?
I don’t know… maybe a little? It’s hard to tell. Even when things are calmer, I don’t always feel that much better right away.
Have these symptoms made it hard for you to keep up with your usual responsibilities?

Yeah… it has. I’m behind on my certificate classes, and stuff at home just kind of piles up—bills, meals, cleaning. My spouse has had to do more than usual. I’ve also been… not really showing up much for friends or art things I’d normally care about.
Even on days when things with your spouse are relatively calm, do you still feel down and uninterested most of the day?

Yeah… even when we’re not fighting, I still feel pretty flat. I don’t really care about the things I usually do—sketching, cooking, yoga, even seeing art or playing tennis with a friend. It just feels like… I don’t have much interest.
Before this started, was there ever a time in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things nearly every day for two weeks or longer?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I’ve had low periods before, but I don’t know if it was nearly every day for two weeks like that.
At any earlier time in your life, did you have a period of at least two weeks when you felt down or lost interest in things nearly every day?
I don’t really know. I’ve had rough patches before, but I can’t say for sure it was every day for two weeks.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a 3-month period of depressive symptoms with persistent anhedonia most days, low mood, fatigue, reduced appetite with unintentional weight loss, impaired concentration/indecisiveness, and clear functional impairment. Although marital conflict is a psychosocial stressor, the depressive syndrome persists even on calmer days and is not clearly limited to or fully explained by adjustment-related mood reactivity. Prior distinct depressive episodes were not established, so recurrent depressive disorder is not supported.
